name: Sword Breath Draw
description: Time the draw to the start of an exhale so the cut leaves the scabbard already carrying a full edge of qi.

name: Steel Breath
description: Hold the breath for one beat and let qi stiffen along the blade so a blow rings off the steel.

name: Exhaled Cut
description: Cut across the target while breathing out so the whole breath goes into the stroke and the edge lands true.

name: Breath Glide
description: Let the breath carry the body a long pace to the side with the blade held level and ready.

name: Sword Surge
description: Surge forward on a long exhale and cut as the feet land so the edge arrives with the weight of the body.

name: Calm Edge
description: Settle the breath and the blade together so a cool shell of qi covers the wielder and sharpens the next cuts.

name: Inner Edge
description: Keep the qi inside the blade until the edge touches the target and release it in a single bright bite.

name: Edge Seed
description: Plant a seed of qi in the steel and let it swell as the wielder breathes so later cuts carry more.

name: Deep Thrust
description: Send the point in with the qi held inside the steel so it pierces further than the blade is long.

name: Edge Pulse
description: Loose the stored qi from the edge as a flat pulse that travels a few paces and stings on arrival.

name: Hidden Edge
description: Hold the blade low and dim with the qi hidden then bring it up in a cut the target did not see coming.

name: Edge Rebound
description: Let the stored qi flare on the flat to push a blade off line and settle again into the steel.

name: Edge Bloom
description: Let the hidden qi bloom outward at the instant of contact so the cut opens wide and rattles the target's grip.

name: Edge Anchor
description: Root the blade with inner qi to stop a heavy blow cold then release the same qi in a short answering cut.

name: Blade Shell
description: Spin the blade before the body until a thin shell of qi forms across the arc and turns light blows.

name: Blade Cover
description: Draw the blade across the body so its qi covers the vitals and takes one hard blow on the flat.

name: Blade Check
description: Check an incoming cut with the edge angled so the blow slides down the steel and off to the side.

name: Guard Pivot
description: Pivot behind the guarding blade to put the body off the line of attack without lowering the sword.

name: Flat Return
description: Swat the flat of the blade back at the striker's wrist right after the guard has caught the blow.

name: Rolling Shell
description: Roll the qi shell along the blade to carry a blow past the body and finish with a cut from the same turn.

name: Sword Lattice
description: Weave the blade in a close lattice of qi that catches many quick cuts at once and holds against all of them.

name: Following Edge
description: Leave the blade where the first cut ended and let its edge follow into the next stroke without a pause.

name: Chain Cut
description: Link two cuts along one arc so the qi of the first rides straight into the second.

name: Second Edge
description: Cut once then return the blade over the same line so the second edge lands where the first opened.

name: Chained Step
description: Step between two cuts so the feet are set before the next stroke leaves the blade.

name: Draw Return
description: Pull the blade back across the body to turn a thrust and send it out again as the next cut.

name: Flowing Guard
description: Move the blade in a slow unbroken curve so a shell of qi follows it round the body.

name: Brief Chain
description: Snap three short thrusts along one line so each carries on from the last without the point leaving it.

name: Tracking Edge
description: Follow the target's guard hand with each cut so every stroke lands where the last one forced it to go.

name: Three Edge Chain
description: Run three cuts together on one breath with the qi passing from edge to edge until the last lands hard.

name: Continuing Ward
description: Turn each parry straight into a cut so the guard never ends and the answering stroke is always already moving.

name: Light Cut
description: Flash a cut so quick that the qi on the edge shines like a streak of white metal.

name: Glint Thrust
description: Show a bright glint at the point to draw the eye and drive the thrust in under it.

name: Bright Parry
description: Flare the edge in the striker's eyes as the flat turns the blow aside.

name: Glintblade Step
description: Step in behind a flash of the blade so the target loses the position of the feet.

name: Sword Gleam
description: Throw a bright sliver of sword qi at the face so the target blinks and the next stroke goes unseen.

name: Radiant Edge
description: Heat the qi on the edge until it glows and cut so the bright line parts guard and flesh alike.

name: Blade Bind
description: Cross blades and press down with a thread of qi along the steel to hold the target's weapon in place.

name: Steel Catch
description: Hook the target's blade on the guard of the sword and wrench it out of line.

name: Cross Hold
description: Hold two crossed blades together under load with qi locked along the crossing until the pressure ends.

name: Press Cut
description: Bear down along the pinned blade and slide the edge into the hand that holds it.

name: Pin Thrust
description: Pin the target's blade with the flat and thrust with the point at the open side of the body.

name: Hilt Lock
description: Catch the target's guard with the quillon and twist so the grip is locked against the wrist.

name: Binding Edge
description: Wind threads of sword qi round the target's blade so it cannot lift and cut the arm that holds it.

name: Sword Tether
description: Hold a line of qi from the point to the target's weapon so it drags with every move and tires its owner.

name: Steel Seal
description: Press the flat to the target's blade and seal the qi in it so the weapon goes dull and heavy.

name: Clean Cut
description: Cut in one pure line with no wasted motion so the qi leaves the edge clean and the wound is narrow.

name: Edge Honing
description: Hone the edge by drawing qi along it in slow strokes so an ally's blade cuts cleaner for several strokes.

name: Steady Guard
description: Hold the blade upright and square so a clean sheet of qi covers the body against one blow.

name: Cutting Step
description: Step across the line of the blow and cut as the foot lands so the edge answers in the same beat.

name: Spine Tap
description: Rap the target's wrist with the back of the blade so the grip loosens and the stroke is spoiled.

name: Cleansing Edge
description: Draw the blade along a comrade's body without touching it and cut the poison or taint out of the blood.

name: Unbinding Edge
description: Cut the binding qi from an ally's limbs with one fine stroke that frees the body and leaves the skin whole.

name: Point Sense
description: Hold the point toward a stranger and let qi run along the blade to feel the reach of the other's weapon.

name: Steel Listening
description: Touch the flat to the other blade and listen for the faint hum that tells how firmly it is held.

name: Reach Mark
description: Cut once at the air and read the edge's return to fix the exact distance of the target's blade.

name: Measured Cut
description: Cut at the exact range the sense has marked so the edge lands at the end of its reach.

name: Marked Thrust
description: Thrust at the weak point the sense has marked in the guard and drive qi in behind the point.

name: Sense Ward
description: Raise a guard at the exact spot the sense warns of so the blow lands on qi rather than on flesh.

name: Seeking Point
description: Let the point slide along the target's guard until the qi finds the gap then drive through it.

name: Hilt Reading
description: Cross blades and read the target's grip tension and shifting hands so the next stroke is known before it comes.
